title: Your Checked Bag's Hidden Ride to the Plane
fb_caption: You drop your bag at the counter and it vanishes. Behind the curtain it rides a maze of belts: its 10-digit barcode tag is read from every side, it's scanned for explosives, and paddles called diverters push it onto your flight's belt at just the right moment. Has an airline ever lost your bag?
engagement_comment: Has an airline ever lost your bag? 1 = never, 2 = once, 3 = I only carry on now.

beats.text: You drop your bag at the counter. It disappears. Here's the ride it takes under the airport.
First, the tag. It carries a ten-digit number, printed as a barcode.
On the belt, lasers and cameras read it from every side, because the bag can land any way up. Some airlines add a radio chip, too.
Then it's scanned for explosives, often while it moves, before it ever reaches the plane.
The computer knows your flight, so paddles called diverters push your bag onto the right belt at the right moment.
It ends in your flight's pile, then rides a cart to the plane's belly.
Has an airline ever lost your bag? Tell us below.
